reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently reviewed complete archived text of 250.010:13376 (subsections 1-2, including subdivisions (1)-(3) in subsection 2) and history notes (L. 1951 p. 638 § 1, A.L. 1983 H.B. 371); verified sourceUrl, sourceSha256, textSha256, and both bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked covered entities (general/special/constitutional charter cities, towns, villages, and chapter 249 or sections 204.250 to 204.470 sewer districts), within-corporate-boundary consent proviso, and chapter-scoped "sewerage system" definition. Revised subsection 1 title to "Sewerage system authority and corporate boundary consent" to avoid narrowing acquisition/construction/improvement/funding/operation to operation alone; retained subsection 2.

headings.title: Sewerage system authority and corporate boundary consent
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1951 p. 638 § 1, A.L. 1983 H.B. 371). Covers authority of cities, towns, villages (general, special, or constitutional charter) and chapter 249 or sections 204.250 to 204.470 sewer districts to acquire, construct, improve, extend, maintain, operate, and fund sewerage systems within or outside corporate boundaries, subject to consent when within corporate boundaries.

headings.title: Meaning of sewerage system for chapter 250
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, including subdivisions (1) to (3), and history note. Covers chapter-scoped definition of sewerage system embracing sewerage systems and treatment plants with appurtenances, combined storm water and sanitary systems, and governing-body-determined storm water sewers relieving undue loads or aiding efficient sanitary sewer operation.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently reviewed complete archived text of 250.060:13382 (subsections 1-3, including subsection 2 ballot template) and history notes (L. 1951 p. 638 § 5, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1621); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Explicitly verified and retained the archived discrepancy in subsection 2's ballot form referencing "(name of city or district)" while subsections 1 and 3 apply only to sewer districts; checked constitutional voter-approval standard and mandatory annual tangible property tax with 20-year bond retirement. Retained all 3 titles.

headings.title: Sewer district tax bonds and voter approval
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1951 p. 638 § 5, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1621). Covers sewer district bonds payable from taxes for improving and extending the district sewerage system, conditioned on approval by the constitutionally required percentage of voters voting on the question.

headings.title: Ballot question form for tax bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, including the ballot template, and history note. Sets out the substantially required ballot question; retains the archived wording referencing '(name of city or district)' even though subsections 1 and 3 refer only to sewer districts.

headings.title: Annual property tax and twenty-year bond retirement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires a sewer district, before incurring indebtedness evidenced by authorized tax bonds, to provide for an annual tax on all taxable tangible property sufficient to pay principal and interest as due and retire the debt within twenty years.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently reviewed complete archived text of 250.070:13383 (subsections 1-2, including subsection 2 ballot template) and history notes (L. 1951 p. 638 § 6, A.L. 1975 H.B. 947, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked distinct voter thresholds (majority for cities/towns/villages vs. four-sevenths for sewer districts) for sewerage or combined system revenue bonds and statutory ballot template. Retained both titles.

headings.title: Voter approval thresholds for revenue bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1951 p. 638 § 6, A.L. 1975 H.B. 947, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971). Prohibits issuing or delivering revenue bonds for sewerage or combined waterworks and sewerage systems without voter assent—a majority for a city, town, or village, or four-sevenths for a sewer district.

headings.title: Ballot question form for revenue bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, including the ballot template, and history note. Prescribes the substantially required ballot question stating the entity name and dollar amount of revenue bonds.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently reviewed complete archived text of 250.080:13384 (subsections 1-6) and history notes (L. 1951 p. 638 § 7, A.L. 1983 H.B. 371); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked ordinance vs. resolution requirement and cost-estimate/bond-term contents, optional early redemption, section 108.170 interest cap, 35-year maturity, and negotiability, bearer/registered/coupon forms, surviving officer signature validity, 90-cents-on-the-dollar price floor, effective interest-cost cap under 108.170, and subordinate bond authority. Revised subsection 1 title to "Authorizing ordinance or resolution and required contents" to cover all required bond terms beyond recitals; retained subsections 2-6.

headings.title: Authorizing ordinance or resolution and required contents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1951 p. 638 § 7, A.L. 1983 H.B. 371). Requires voter-approved revenue bonds to be issued by municipal ordinance or district resolution reciting a cost estimate and setting out bond amount, purposes, dates, denominations, interest rates, payment times and places, and other details.

headings.title: Optional redemption prior to maturity
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Permits revenue bonds to be subject to redemption before maturity, with or without premium, at times and on conditions set by the governing body.

headings.title: Interest rate under 108.170, maturity, and negotiability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Governs interest rates in accordance with section 108.170, the thirty-five-year maximum maturity, and status of chapter 250 bonds as negotiable instruments under the negotiable instruments act.

headings.title: Bearer, registered, and coupon bond forms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Permits bonds to be payable to bearer, registered, or coupon bonds, with principal-and-interest or principal-only registration privileges as provided in the authorizing ordinance or resolution.

headings.title: Bond signing and validity of officer signatures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Directs signing of bonds and coupons as specified by ordinance or resolution and preserves signature validity even if a signing officer leaves office before delivery or did not hold office on the date ascribed to the bonds.

headings.title: Sale terms, price and rate limits, and subordinate bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Covers governing-body sale terms, the minimum ninety-cents-on-the-dollar sale price, the section 108.170 effective interest-cost cap on actual proceeds, and optional authorization of junior or subordinate revenue bonds.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently reviewed complete archived text of 250.120:13388 (subsections 1-4) and history note (L. 1951 p. 638 § 11); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked mandatory rate-fixing/revision duty while revenue bonds remain outstanding, irrelevance of prior free service or original financing, private water company data duty in subsection 4, and the party distinction in subsection 3 authorizing only "the city, town or village" (not sewer districts) to discontinue water service for combined-system nonpayment. Revised subsection 3 title to "Combined system rates and municipal water disconnection" to preserve that city-only wording faithfully; retained subsections 1, 2, and 4.

headings.title: Duty to fix, revise, and collect sufficient rates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1951 p. 638 § 11). Establishes a revenue-bond issuer's mandatory duty to fix, maintain, periodically revise, and collect rates sufficient for maintenance, operation, bond principal and interest, and valid ordinance or resolution requirements while bonds remain outstanding.

headings.title: Rates regardless of prior free service or financing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires rates to be fixed and charged regardless of whether services were previously provided free or how the system was originally financed.

headings.title: Combined system rates and municipal water disconnection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Allows separate or combined water and sewer charges for combined systems and authorizes 'the city, town or village' (without naming sewer districts in the disconnection clause) to discontinue water service upon failure to pay within a reasonable time.

headings.title: Basing sewerage rates on private water company data
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Permits basing sewerage rates in whole or part on water supplied by a private water company and imposes a duty on that private water company to furnish necessary calculation information.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently reviewed complete archived text of 250.130:13389 (subsections 1-3) and history note (L. 1951 p. 638 § 13); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked statutory net-revenue pledge for sewerage or combined system revenue bonds, definition of "net revenues" after actual/necessary O&M expenses, and mandatory custodial officials' payment duty. Retained all 3 titles.

headings.title: Statutory pledge of net revenues for revenue bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1951 p. 638 § 13). Pledges by operation of chapter 250 a sufficient amount of net revenues of the sewerage or combined system to pay principal and interest on issued revenue bonds as they mature and accrue.

headings.title: Meaning of net revenues
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Construes 'net revenues' as all operating revenues of the system less actual and necessary expenses of operation and maintenance.

headings.title: Officials' duty to provide prompt bond payment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Places a mandatory duty on municipal or sewer district officials charged with custody and management of system revenues to provide for prompt payment of maturing principal and accruing interest.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently reviewed complete archived text of 250.140:13390 (subsections 1-5) and history notes (L. 1951 p. 638 § 12, A.L. 2002 S.B. 932, A.L. 2005 H.B. 58 merged with S.B. 210); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked chapter 247 water supply district inclusion, subsection 2 exception, 30-day good-faith delinquency notice, 90-day owner cap and archived pre-January 1, 2007 120-day transitional proviso for St. Louis City and qualifying multi-county home rule cities >400,000, private-line scope vs. shared-line owner liability, water provider termination immunity, and unapplied-for utility services exclusion/definition. Revised subsection 1 title to "Occupant and owner liability and collection suits" to avoid inserting the unstated label "Joint"; retained subsections 2-5.

headings.title: Occupant and owner liability and collection suits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1951 p. 638 § 12, A.L. 2002 S.B. 932, A.L. 2005 H.B. 58 merged with S.B. 210). Deems sewerage, water, or combined services furnished to both occupant and owner and, subject to subsection 2, empowers municipalities, sewer districts, and chapter 247 water supply districts to sue either or both for sums due less held deposits plus court-fixed reasonable attorney's fees.

headings.title: Delinquency notices, owner liability caps, and termination notices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers good-faith 30-day delinquency notice to owners, the 90-day owner liability cap, the archived historical pre-January 1, 2007 120-day cap for St. Louis City and qualifying multi-county home rule cities over 400,000 inhabitants, and sending termination notices to both occupant and owner.

headings.title: Private-line applicability and shared-line owner liability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Limits section 250.140 to residences with their own private water and sewer lines and assigns liability to the real property owner when several residences share a common water or sewer line.

headings.title: Water provider immunity for delinquency termination
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Grants immunity from civil or criminal damages to any water provider terminating service due to a consumer's payment delinquency, notwithstanding other law.

headings.title: Exclusion and meaning of unapplied-for utility services
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Excludes unapplied-for utility services from section 250.140, defines the term as services requiring property-owner application and utility acceptance before account establishment, and notes direct billing and delinquency responsibility of the property owner rather than occupant.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently reviewed complete archived text of 250.150:13391 (subsections 1-2, including subdivisions (1)-(4) in subsection 1) and history note (L. 1951 p. 638 § 14); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked revenue/bank-account segregation, five-tier payment priority order, separate accounting and annual public-accountant audits open to taxpayers/users/bondholders, duty performance, and strict prerequisites for transferring operating funds or paying non-system obligations. Retained both titles.

headings.title: Revenue segregation, payment priority, audits, and duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, including subdivisions (1) to (4), and history note (L. 1951 p. 638 § 14). Details mandatory duties for rate-collecting municipalities and sewer districts: segregating system funds and bank accounts, following a five-tier payment priority order, maintaining separate accounts with annual public-accountant audits open to taxpayer/user/bondholder inspection, and performing legal and bond-ordinance duties.

headings.title: Conditions for transferring revenues and paying other obligations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Prohibits transferring system operating funds to other entity funds without governing-body action and full payment of operating expenses, due bond principal and interest, money covenants, and due revenue obligations, and bars paying other debts or expenses from system revenues absent a qualifying transfer.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently reviewed complete archived text of 250.160:13392 (subsections 1-3, including subdivisions (1)-(7) in subsection 1) and history note (L. 1951 p. 638 § 15); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked non-exhaustive list of separate revenue accounts in bond ordinances, in-state or out-of-state bank/trust-company trust deposits, and authority to limit additional revenue bonds and include protective covenants. Retained all 3 titles.

headings.title: Authorizing separate revenue accounts in bond ordinances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, including subdivisions (1) to (7), and history note (L. 1951 p. 638 § 15). Permits revenue-bond ordinances to allocate system revenues periodically into separate accounts, listing non-exhaustive examples for operation and maintenance, bond payments, depreciation reserves, payment reserves, contingencies, extensions and improvements, and other desirable accounts.

headings.title: Depositing bond payment and reserve funds in trust accounts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Permits holding bond-payment or reserve account sums on deposit as a trust account in a bank or trust company located within or outside Missouri.

headings.title: Limits on additional bonds and protective covenants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Permits bond ordinances to limit additional revenue bonds or their holders' rights and to include agreements, covenants, or restrictions safeguarding bondholder interests and securing payment.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently reviewed complete archived text of 250.170:13393 (subsections 1-2) and history note (L. 1951 p. 638 § 16); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked standing of bondholders and accrued interest-coupon holders to bring actions at law or equity (mandamus, injunction, or otherwise), and confirmed subsection 2 conditions pre-default suits on neglect or failure to perform a material legal duty or valid bond-ordinance covenant. Revised subsection 2 title to "Actions for material neglect without prior bond default" so the statutory trigger is explicit; retained subsection 1.

headings.title: Bondholder actions to compel performance of duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1951 p. 638 § 16). Authorizes bondholders or interest-coupon holders to bring civil actions at law or equity (mandamus, injunction, or otherwise) to compel municipalities, sewer districts, or officials to perform statutory and bond-ordinance duties including system operation, rate fixing, revenue segregation, bond payment, and valid covenants.

headings.title: Actions for material neglect without prior bond default
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Allows such actions regardless of whether any bond or interest is in default at filing if the entity or an official neglected or failed to perform a material legal duty or valid covenant.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently reviewed complete archived text of 250.200:13395 (subsections 1-3), history note (L. 1951 p. 638 § 19), and Revisor footnote (*Words "waste from" substituted for "was to form" in enrolled bill, referenced in subsections 1 and 2); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked revenue-bond prerequisite, active sewer-connection trigger in overlapping municipal and sewer-district territory, and subsection 3's dual-charge bar and first-imposed priority rule. Retained all 3 titles.

headings.title: Municipal rates on overlapping sewer district territory
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history note (L. 1951 p. 638 § 19), and Revisor footnote (*Words 'waste from' substituted for 'was to form' in enrolled bill). Requires revenue-bond-issuing cities, towns, or villages embracing sewer district territory directly served by the municipal system to impose and collect rates on actively connected premises even if district facilities also carry the waste.

headings.title: Sewer district rates on overlapping municipal territory
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history note, and Revisor footnote (*Words 'waste from' substituted for 'was to form' in enrolled bill). Requires revenue-bond-issuing sewer districts embracing municipal territory to impose and collect rates on premises actively connected to the district system even if municipal facilities also carry the waste.

headings.title: Prohibition on dual charges and first-imposed priority
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Bars both the municipality and sewer district from charging the same lot, parcel, or premises for sewerage services, giving priority to whichever political subdivision first imposed rates and charges.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently reviewed complete archived text of 250.236:13403 (subsections 1-2) and history notes (L. 1992 S.B. 470 & 497 § 1, A.L. 2001 H.B. 501, A.L. 2011 S.B. 48); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked municipal contract authority with private or public water companies, >3-month arrears and customer-notice prerequisites, and explicitly verified the archived wording distinction in subsection 2 granting termination-damages immunity to "A private or public water company" while directing cost reimbursement to "the private water company" (retained without inventing a correction). Revised subsection 2 title to "Water company immunity and private-company cost reimbursement" to mirror the archived statutory scope accurately; retained subsection 1.

headings.title: Contracts and conditions for water or sewer disconnection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 470 & 497 § 1, A.L. 2001 H.B. 501, A.L. 2011 S.B. 48). Permits cities, towns, or villages to contract with private or public water companies to terminate water service for unpaid sewer bills, and authorizes sewer disconnection or written water-termination requests after more than three months of arrears and customer notice until charges and related costs are paid.

headings.title: Water company immunity and private-company cost reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Exempts a private or public water company acting on a subsection 1 written request from damages liability for terminating water service, and requires city reimbursement of disconnection and reconnection costs to 'the private water company' (noting the archived text specifies 'private' in the reimbursement sentence while naming 'private or public' in the immunity sentence).
